content:
SECTION 1

* A young person (Sam Webb, age 24) is frustrated that older generations criticize young people for spending money on things like holidays or restaurants instead of saving every penny for a house.

* He points out that houses in the UK have become so expensive and hard to buy that most young people will probably never be able to afford one, even if they save.

* Young workers under 25 years old get paid much less than older workers for doing the exact same job - someone aged 18-20 can legally be paid only £5.60 per hour.

* A 24-year-old working full-time might only earn about £14,500 per year, which makes it nearly impossible to save enough money to buy a house.

* The writer feels trapped in a cycle where young people must rent forever, giving all their money to landlords, while those same property owners complain that young people are financially irresponsible.
